newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gle Eaux head rules out buying rival TV.
newsitem.headline: Gle Eaux head rules out buying rival TV.

text.p: Jean-Marie Messier, chairman of France's Cie Generale des Eaux, ruled out buying TF1, a rival to its indirectly-controlled pay TV unit Canal Plus in an interview with the daily newspaper Liberation published on Friday.

Asked if he would be a candidate to buy TF1, France's biggest private television station, Messier said: "Not in any circumstances, because that does not correspond at all to my industrial strategy. We are trying to build a multimedia group and not a television company."
He said he would wait calmly for the market's judgement on which digital satellite television service, TF1's Television par Satellite (TPS) or Canal Plus's Canalsatellite, would win out.
"We need 18 months to see clearly in German broadcasting, in the balance of forces between Canalsatellite and TPS or in the relations between Havas and Canal Plus with CLT-UFA," he said.

Belgian financier Albert Frere, whose CLT last year merged with UFA, the broadcasting arm of Germany's Bertelsmann, is the only shareholder who still has a stake in both Havas and in Lyonnaise des Eaux.
Havas is controlled by Generale des Eaux and is itself the biggest shareholder in Canal Plus. Lyonnaise des Eaux rivals Generale des Eaux in telecommunications and television.
"With Albert Frere I am convinced we will not stay in the current situation," Messier said.
Messier contested Culture and Communication Minister Catherine Trautmann's recent assertion that concentration was key in the media sector.
"In this business, what represents influence is not the concentration of capital but the audience level. We are far from having reached critical mass," he said.
"It is not enough to catch new subscribers, you have to keep them. And we work in businesses with fixed costs and there will not be room for everybody," he said.
